review_notes:
I read the whole file and the Mathlib definitions it depends on. Those were `GroupExtension.Section`, `surjInvRightHom`, `conjAct`, `inl_conjAct_comm` and `mul_mul_mul_inv_mem_range_inl`. Every statement is already stated for arbitrary groups N, G, Q and an arbitrary extension S and section σ, so nothing is tied to a concrete type.

The two normalisation lemmas `factor_one_left` and `factor_one_right` assume `σ 1 = 1`. That assumption is what the conclusion needs. Without it, `factor S σ 1 q` has the form σ 1 · σ q · σ q⁻¹, which is not trivial in general. Weakening the hypothesis would not give a clean statement.

One minor variant is possible. `normalizedExtensionSection` could normalise an arbitrary section σ instead of only `S.surjInvRightHom`. I judged this too marginal to report, because the file gives no use that needs it. The Mathlib definitions are stated only for groups, so relaxing the group classes to monoids is not an option. I found no useful unreported generalisation.
